coachingObservations: The scoring line has zero depth and sits exactly on the end line (space.regions[c:restated:GF2:GF2-03.e].position.along = 0). That is what the knowledge entails for a line, and it is physically markable — but a coach may expect a scoring zone with some depth, and the game does not give one.

The scoring line has zero depth and sits exactly on the end line (space.regions[c:restated:GF2:GF2-03.f].position.along = 40). That is what the knowledge entails for a line, and it is physically markable — but a coach may expect a scoring zone with some depth, and the game does not give one.

The game DOES establish an initial holder of possession, and the activity cannot tell a coach which team it is. The two teams are indiscernible — identical but for an internal handle that must not reach coach-facing text — so the holder identifies a member without describing one. It matters because a transition is keyed on a change of possession, so it decides which team is attacking in the first episode of play. It is a knowledge gap and not a rendering one: nothing authors anything that tells the two teams apart.

2 `functions` row(s) are simply NOT CONSTRAINED — nothing authored says what those regions are "for" and nothing forbids saying it either (space.regions[c:restated:GF2:GF2-03.e].functions; space.regions[c:restated:GF2:GF2-03.f].functions). That is an absence of knowledge rather than an authored exclusion, and it does not stop a region participating: this game's target region participates because the objective references it, not because it carries a function string.

Realization chose "line" among ["zone","line"] for space.regions[c:restated:GF2:GF2-03.e].noun, space.regions[c:restated:GF2:GF2-03.f].noun. The alternative not taken ("zone") is not offered to the coach: no approved wording describes it, and saying it would need facts the game does not hold.

Realization chose "line_crossed" among ["line_crossed","target_zone_entered"] for value.primaryEvent.kind. The alternative not taken ("target_zone_entered") is not offered to the coach: no approved wording describes it, and saying it would need facts the game does not hold.

check.because: B4, 28 October 2026 (ours; R8's E4a). Until now only an activity whose provisional realization declares defaultLawsCheck was held to the account, so a composed activity gained none. This check is the sport's, held only to a Learning Goal's activity whose realization declares no check of its own (a realization's own check wins; engineering demonstrations are never held). Each adaptation the account finds owed is MATERIAL, and the activity is refused before it is served, or PROCEDURAL, and it is reported for review and refuses nothing. An owed adaptation no classification names counts as MATERIAL (fail safe). No classification is held here or anywhere in production knowledge: our classification of these laws is a DRAFT for his review (docs/audits/drafts/laws-materiality.DRAFT.json), read only by composition-test builds, so in production every owed adaptation counts as MATERIAL.

words: For offside and other Laws of the Game adaptations, normal rules remain the starting point, with explicit modifications where necessary.
For the general Laws check, I favor this distinction:
Material unresolved conflicts affecting the activity's meaning, safety, or structural validity should prevent approval.
Minor or nonessential procedural questions may be reported for review without stopping development.
We should avoid another extended investigation into every possible soccer rule before establishing the activity's essential design.

source.editionNote: He names no edition. The laws are cited by IFAB law number only, and nothing here depends on an edition's wording; the d26 design read Laws 1 and 12 from theifab.com, which showed the 2026/27 edition as current. Which edition governs is his to name.

words: The normal Laws of the Game should apply by default wherever they are applicable, unless an activity introduces an explicit, knowledge-authorized modification.
We should not need to redefine ordinary soccer rules separately for every Learning Goal, game form, or activity.

Where a normal law cannot apply directly because of the modified field, scoring structure, or game format, the system should identify the relevant adaptation rather than silently assume conventional conditions exist.
The offside question, for example, may need an explicit ruling for this small-sided environment, but we should not expand the current work into a comprehensive reconstruction of soccer's laws.
The governing principle is to inherit established sport rules and explicitly define only the necessary departures.

laws.name: the goalkeeper's handling
laws.note: His reply filed 26 October 2026, item 7: "The goalkeeper's handling permissions and restrictions should follow the normal Laws of the Game within that area unless an authorized activity rule explicitly changes them." The region-function token 'penalty-area' is ours (DRAFT); since 23 October 2026 (H3, register version 21) it is a member of the register's region-function list, and the boundRegions block below binds it to a defended goal, with the regulation pairing alone authorized. The penalty area's geometry for any other goal is decision 1 of the note sent to him, and handling in the zone version is decision 5. Where a goalkeeper plays and no penalty area exists, the law's purpose remains, so an adaptation is owed. AMENDED 24 October 2026 (the completeness audit of the field-test build, item 2): 'with the regulation pairing alone authorized' and 'The penalty area's geometry for any other goal is decision 1 of the note sent to him' are no longer true. Since K1 (24 October 2026) the boundRegions block also authorizes the FA 5v5 pairing (FA-MINI-SOCCER-5V5-2026) for its goal, his reply filed 27 October 2026, item 1: "I agree with using an established small-sided goal and its corresponding penalty area as the starting configuration for the 40 × 30 m activity." "I also approve your proposed general principle in 1b: a goal’s penalty-area geometry should ordinarily come from the same authorized format. Any exception should be explicit and supported by the intended learning design." Since K2 the goal version records that pairing's penalty area, and since K3 its account records this law as applying in both blocks. Handling in the zone version is still his (his reply filed 27 October 2026, item 5: "I would not finalize your proposed feet-only interpretation yet." "For now, preserve the validated target-zone version without silently adding new handling restrictions."), so the zone version still owes this law. AMENDED 24 October 2026 (the completeness audit of the field-test build, item 1): the DRAFT clause telling the coach to give the goalkeeper a colour neither team wears, written for this law at stage L, is written for LAW-4-GK (the goalkeeper's colours, below) since this audit, so it no longer rests on this law applying; only the handling clause inside the penalty area does. AMENDED 25 October 2026 (Z, register version 25): its requirement read REGION_BOUND_TO_OBJECT {function: penalty-area, kind: goal} (a penalty area bound to a goal) until today; it now reads REGION_OF_PERFORMER {function: penalty-area, row: P3}: a penalty area belonging to the team holding the goalkeeper, bound to a goal that team defends (register row O7), as in the goal version, or, where no goal stands at that team's end, to that team's own end line (register row S7's second form; the boundRegions block's BOUND-REGION-PERFORMER-END), for his reply filed 28 October 2026, item 7 ("7. Goalkeeper handling in the target-zone version"): "I favor retaining a defined goalkeeper handling area in the target-zone version." "The absence of a physical goal shouldn't automatically eliminate the goalkeeper's handling privileges or fundamentally alter the player's functional role during the build-out." "My preference is to use the same authorized small-sided penalty-area geometry where appropriate, even when the physical goal is replaced by a target zone." Law 12 gives the goalkeeper's handling inside its own penalty area, which the new predicate states directly. 'so the zone version still owes this law' is no longer true: the zone version (A01-R1) now holds the goalkeeper's penalty area at the goalkeeper's own end in each block (A01-R1-S2-2, S5-5, S6-2, S6-3, S7-1), so its account records this law as applying in both blocks and owes nothing. The goal version's account reads exactly as before (APPLIES in each block). The predicate's name is ours (DRAFT).

laws.name: the goalkeeper's colours
laws.note: Listed 24 October 2026 (the completeness audit of the field-test build, item 1). IFAB Law 4.3, as the d27 design's stage L cited it: "Each goalkeeper must wear colours that are distinguishable from the other players and the match officials" (https://www.theifab.com/laws/latest/the-players-equipment/). His reply filed 27 October 2026, item 6, agreeing with the reading our 26 October email put to him for no one version ("The goalkeeper wears their own colour (Law 4), so at an exchange only an outfield player who transfers changes bib (no one, with 11 players)."): "Goalkeeper identification: The goalkeeper should be visually distinguishable from the outfield players. Stable team identities and clear role labels remain important in the diagram." Why it is listed, and for ADAPTATION, is OUR READING of his reply filed 26 October 2026, item 10 ("Where a normal law cannot apply directly because of the modified field, scoring structure, or game format, the system should identify the relevant adaptation rather than silently assume conventional conditions exist."): in a training activity no match kit can be assumed, and where the goalkeeper changes team at a role exchange (both build-out versions) no shirt of either team tells the goalkeeper apart, so the activity must tell the coach how. That is the DRAFT clause written for this law (docs/audits/draft-coach-wording.json, appliedLaws: 'give the {performer} a colour neither team wears'), said at the end of the Players sentence wherever the game's default-laws account records this law as applying, and required there by fidelity. It arises wherever a team holds a goalkeeper (applicableWhen) and needs nothing the representation holds (no row records what a performer wears), so it is never owed: where a goalkeeper plays it APPLIES, and elsewhere it is NOT_APPLICABLE. Like every law here it is read only for a game whose realization declares defaultLawsCheck (on 24 October 2026 the two build-out versions, A01-R1 and A01-R2); a game with no account says nothing of it. Until this entry the clause was written for LAW-12-GK, the goalkeeper's handling, and so was said only where that law applies (the goal version); that the colour belongs with handling was OUR READING (the d27 design's 3.7(e): the colour shows who may handle), and his item 6 limits it to no version. The FA's Mini-Soccer handbook asks only for a shirt of a different colour from the rest of the goalkeeper's own team, so it is not cited for 'neither team'. The id and the name are ours (DRAFT).
